qc.label_under_test: 'either' (or German entw|eder) opening an either...or choice between two options: the pole marks the start of a correlative disjunction; 'either' at the end of a negative clause, and the same choices written with plain 'or', stay low

neighbours.label: The opening word of a correlative pair: 'both', 'either', 'not only', 'not just', which promises a second element to come
fire: The program helps both students and teachers in town.
You can reach us either by phone or by letter.
The mayor not only read the report but also signed it.
Their new plan covers both rent and food.
The dish is not just cheap but also tasty.
Guests may choose either the fish or the lamb.
She speaks both French and German at home.
The shop is not only open late but also close by.
quiet: The program helps students and teachers in town.
You can reach us by phone or by letter.
The mayor read the report and also signed it.
Their new plan covers rent and food.
The dish is cheap and also tasty.
We don't serve the lamb either.
She speaks French and German at home.
The shop isn't open late either.

predictions: The opening word fires. The same pairs without it, and 'either' at the end of a negative clause, stay low.
